name: view_as_real_copy
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::view_as_real_copy(Tensor self) -> Tensor. This is one registered overload only; it is not exclusive and does not narrow the operator contract. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: it defines every overload, keyword argument, return value, error, aliasing and mutation behavior, and no test may be removed or have its reference behavior adapted to fit this single signature. Other registered schema strings supplied for this operator, verbatim: aten::view_as_real_copy(Tensor self) -> Tensor ; aten::view_as_real_copy.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics derived from the tests: given a complex tensor, the operator returns a freshly allocated, contiguous real tensor whose trailing dimension is 2 and whose last-axis pairs are the real and imaginary components; for non-empty inputs the tests check that the result does not share the input's base storage, and a mutation case shows that a write on either side does not reach the other. The tested inputs are complex only; the negative cases feed real, bool, integer and float8 dtypes (each included only when the device supports it) and expect RuntimeError from the tested implementation. A lazily conjugated input is accepted rather than rejected, its values match the resolved reference, and the input keeps its conjugate bit; this pytest calls only aten::view_as_real_copy, so no behavior of aten::view_as_real is asserted here. Transpose, offset and sliced inputs are copied element-wise rather than read as packed storage, while a zero-stride broadcast input is exercised only together with a conjugate bit; empty shapes yield empty results. The out overload (keyword-only out, mutated, aliased return) writes the components at the caller buffer's own offsets and keeps the caller's layout; the call returns the out object itself, and for the tested complex64 input an out buffer whose dtype is not that input's real component dtype (float16, int32, complex64, and float64 where supported) raises RuntimeError. Backward folds a real gradient of shape shape+(2,) back into the complex input. Overload-dependent behavior of the out variant is described here rather than modeled conditionally.
